subject: Follow-up: residency constraints & hosting options for PanAsia pilot
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@panasia-ins.com>, Tom Yuen <tom.yuen@cloudprocure.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: residency constraints & hosting options for PanAsia pilot

Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can move to a scoped pilot:  

Recap
- Primary goal: pilot PanAsia customer-facing classification service for claims intake (low-latency inference for text).
- Residency constraint: EU customers must keep raw PII and inference artifacts inside EU boundaries; APAC customers (notably Japan) have stricter residency expectations.
- Traffic profile: you mentioned a mix of EU-heavy + smaller APAC base (details below).

Clarifying questions (so the pilot configuration is correct) — can you confirm the following:  
1) Rough traffic split for pilot (we discussed ~60% EU / ~25% APAC / ~15% other) — please confirm percentages and any country-specific rules (e.g., Japan must not leave country).
2) For Japan: is a customer-managed VPC or on-prem requirement mandatory, or would a dedicated capacity located in Japan (customer data never egressing) be acceptable?
3) Are there any contractual constraints around cross-region failover? You noted you prefer not to fall back to US regions — is that a hard constraint or negotiable for disaster recovery?
4) Compliance docs: which artifacts should we send first (SOC 2 + encryption summary is attached; we can also pull in data flow diagrams if helpful).

Options we propose (high level) — we'll align on the pilot based on your answers above:  
- Hosted (regional tenancy): Redwood Hosted API with EU and APAC region tenancy; good for fastest time-to-value but requires strict routing rules to avoid cross-region egress.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in a region): predictable throughput and stronger isolation; can be provisioned in Tokyo and Frankfurt to satisfy residency without VPC networking changes.
- Private VPC / on-prem: customer-managed network and routing — recommended where law requires customer-controlled keying/routing (higher ops overhead).

Next steps (proposed)
- I attached SOC2-Summary-2026.pdf and a short deployment-matrix.csv that maps options to tradeoffs.
- Please reply with Q1–Q3 above by EOD Wed 1/20 so Marissa and Vivek can size the pilot accurately.
- If the answers indicate Japan requires customer VPC/on-prem, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive to scope network handoffs and router ACLs (Marissa/Vivek to lead).

Thanks — looking forward to confirming the pilot configuration.

—
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: Follow-up: residency constraints & hosting options for PanAsia pilot

Thanks Rishi — useful recap. A few clarifications below (inline answers):

On Mon, 18 Jan 2027 at 13:12, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Rough traffic split for pilot (we discussed ~60% EU / ~25% APAC / ~15% other) — please confirm percentages and any country-specific rules (e.g., Japan must not leave country).

We confirm: EU ~62% (majority DE/FR), APAC ~24 (Japan ~14, Singapore ~10), Other ~14 (US + UK non-production).
Japan has a strict requirement: raw PII and model inputs/outputs for Japan-originating requests must not be exported outside Japan. For the pilot that is a hard constraint — we cannot have those requests routed through a US or EU compute instance.

> 2) For Japan: is a customer-managed VPC or on-prem requirement mandatory, or would a dedicated capacity located in Japan (customer data never egressing) be acceptable?

A dedicated capacity located in Japan with contractual guarantee of no egress is acceptable and preferable to full on-prem for the pilot. For production we may need to revisit.

> 3) Are there any contractual constraints around cross-region failover? You noted you prefer not to fall back to US regions — is that a hard constraint or negotiable for disaster recovery?

For Japan-originating traffic: no cross-region failover allowed outside Japan except in documented DR events that we approve in advance. For EU-originating traffic we have more flexibility (can accept EU fallback to another EU region).

> 4) Compliance docs: which artifacts should we send first (SOC 2 + encryption summary is attached; we can also pull in data flow diagrams if helpful).

Please send SOC2 and an encryption-at-rest/transport summary first. Also include a high-level network diagram showing ingress points by region (if you can redact internal IPs that's fine).

We'll aim to respond to the rest of the checklist by EOD Wed (1/20). Can you propose 2 slots for the technical deep-dive (we prefer mornings JST for our infra team)?

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Hoffman
Head of Platform Security | PanAsia Insurance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@panasia-ins.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 16:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: residency constraints & hosting options for PanAsia pilot

Hi Lena — looping in technical details and tradeoffs for your infra team.

Short answer: we can support the architecture you described, but the recommended pilot configurations differ by strictness requirement.

Options (tradeoffs)
- Hosted (regional tenancy): We operate eu-central and asia-southeast regions. For EU-origin requests we can ensure processing remains in eu-central when routing/policies are set. Hosted is fastest to stand up but does not provide customer-managed network controls; good if contractual guarantees and logs suffice.

- Dedicated capacity (regional): We can provision Dedicated capacity in a Tokyo availability zone so Japan-origin traffic never leaves Japan. Dedicated provides stronger isolation and is normally sufficient wherever laws allow compute to be managed by provider but not exported. Cost is higher than Hosted but lower operational overhead than a full VPC/on-prem.

- Private VPC / On-prem: If you require customer-managed networking or on-prem key management (HSM), Private VPC or on-prem will be necessary. Higher engineering integration and longer lead time.

Network & failure assumptions
- Default hosted fallback: we do not fall back to US regions for EU/APAC traffic unless explicitly configured; fallback is configurable per-route.
- For Japan strict-residency: we recommend Dedicated Tokyo for pilot; set a manual-runbook for DR and a documented approval process for any out-of-country failover.

Attachments: I updated deployment-matrix.csv to add an explicit Tokyo-dedicated row and a one-page checklist for the pilot.

If you confirm Dedicated Tokyo is acceptable for pilot, Vivek and I will prepare a sizing estimate and a timeline (provisioning + validation + canary).

—
Marissa Cole
Product Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
